definitions.explanation: A vertical structural support in a building. In traditional Japanese architecture, wooden pillars are essential elements.
A person or thing that provides essential support.

examples.japanese: この{家|いえ}は{太|ふと}い{柱|はしら}で{支|ささ}えられています。
examples.english: This house is supported by thick pillars.

examples.japanese: {柱|はしら}に{身長|しんちょう}を{記録|きろく}しました。
examples.english: I marked my height on the pillar.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}はチームの{大黒柱|だいこくばしら}です。
examples.english: He is the mainstay of the team.

notes:
{柱|はしら} refers to pillars and columns.

Types in traditional architecture:
- {大黒柱|だいこくばしら} (main pillar, also "mainstay")
- {床柱|とこばしら} (alcove pillar in tokonoma)
- {通|とお}し{柱|ばしら} (continuous pillar through floors)

Cultural significance:
- In traditional homes, {大黒柱|だいこくばしら} is central and sacred
- Children's height often marked on pillars as family memory
- Fine wood species used for visible pillars

Figurative expressions:
- {大黒柱|だいこくばしら} (main pillar/breadwinner of family)
- {柱|はしら}となる (to become a pillar/mainstay)
- {四本柱|しほんばしら} (four pillars - sumo ring)

Counter for pillars: {本|ほん}
Counter for gods/spirits: {柱|はしら} (archaic/literary)
